pr_title: apiserver: disable info level gRPC logging
pr_body:
gRPC balancer wrapper has (non-leveled) info logging on "Notify" call.
Which maens we are logging every single endpoint resolution.
When the cluster scales up, the logging for apiserver can dramatically
increase.

Since etcd v3 client already provides all the relevant information,
let's disable gRPC info logging to reduce the log size.

Signed-off-by: Gyuho Lee <leegyuho@amazon.com>

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Disable gRPC info-level logging. We need it to reduce the logging size. We don't need these logs:

```
I1017 18:22:59.790791       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: []
I1017 18:22:59.790877       6 controlbuf.go:382] transport: loopyWriter.run returning. connection error: desc = "transport is closing"
I1017 18:22:59.790986       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{...:2379 <nil>}]
I1017 18:22:59.791038       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{...:2379 <nil>}]
I1017 18:22:59.793949       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{...:2379 <nil>}]
```

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80741

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Disable gRPC info level logging
```

issue_context.body:

I0730 15:38:27.137684       1 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{etcd.xxx.com:2379 <nil>}]
I0730 15:38:27.137709       1 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{etcd.xxx.com:2379 <nil>}]
I0730 15:38:27.137733       1 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{etcd.xxx.com:2379 <nil>}]
I0730 15:38:27.142843       1 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{etcd.xxx.com:2379 <nil>}]

(10+ lines / 20s)

etcd.xxx.com is LB of etcd cluster
kube-apiserver version is 1.14.3 
i found that cluster can work normally
so ,how can i close those logs??

This is from vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/balancer_v1_wrapper.go

Maybe surface to grpc project ?
I meet this problem too, k8s version is 1.15.1

We do set the gRPC logger by default, in etcd

https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/a65e4d3357c260504d47f08a433b355e36dbcb51/clientv3/logger.go#L36-L40

to ignore all such logs.

@jpbetz @liggitt Do we override gRPC logger somewhere in kube-apiserver?

I tried

```
env:
- name: GRPC_GO_LOG_SEVERITY_LEVEL
  value: warning
```

but no luck...

```
I1017 18:22:59.790791       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: []
I1017 18:22:59.790877       6 controlbuf.go:382] transport: loopyWriter.run returning. connection error: desc = "transport is closing"
I1017 18:22:59.790986       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{...:2379 <nil>}]
I1017 18:22:59.791038       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{...:2379 <nil>}]
I1017 18:22:59.793949       6 asm_amd64.s:1337] balancerWrapper: got update addr from Notify: [{...:2379 <nil>}]
```
should we adjust the klog adapter to make all info-level logs from etcd a higher verbosity (e.g. V3 or V4?)

@liggitt I think we need a way to disable the whole `Info` level logging in `klog` package. Can we translate the kube-apiserver log level to gRPC log writer? Seems like gRPC doesn't really use leveled logging. For example, even if we set the log level, this line will still print:

https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/7c8e60372e19da88fb3fe8ac6a8de781eef7f547/balancer_v1_wrapper.go#L116

which runs for every single gRPC connection.

To discard info level logging in gRPC, we can pass `ioutil.Discard` to `grpclog.NewLoggerV2` or `grpclog.NewLoggerV2WithVerbosity`. Or implement this to the `klog`?
On second thought, I don't think we need gRPC info level logs at all. etcd client is migrating to zap logger, and it logs all the critical information.

review_comments: I didn't expect to send things directly to os.Stderr... that doesn't get seen by things that expected to direct error logs to a file
Is log writer configurable in kube-apiserver? If we expose log writer from `klog`, so we emit logs to the same writer for warning and error messages from gRPC. Or pase `--logtostderr` flag?

As Gyuho pointed offline, it seems like this is similar to what we're doing in etcd server as well - https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/bf3d1fb48429a0050f82b5b3233d86903009b327/embed/config_logging.go#L104

> Is log writer configurable in kube-apiserver?

Yes, via klog flags

Do we have other grpc clients that would be affected by this? cc @immutableT for storage encryption client

Instead of exporting these fields, you could add an exported method that could be used to retrieve this information for callers that need to determine log configuration.

Alternately, you could also add this override directly into the klog package itself, possible with some flag to control the override? What do you think @dims?
[Loggerv2](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/grpclog#LoggerV2) is an interface, why can we not also use a klog wrapper here?
